text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- More than 60 percent of adult Poles feel unsafe due to crime growth in the last few years, a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Around 68 percent of Poles say they will vote in the parliamentary elections in September, a survey by the CBOS polling institute in July showed.
The survey's favourites were the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) with support of 24 percent of Poles and the right-wing Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), supported by 23 percent.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPLITA

- Duty free import quotas related to repairing damage caused by floods will only include chemical and specialist equipment directly used in flood removal operations, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.
- The state-owned PZU insurance firm will pay 568 million zlotys in damages to flood victims in southern Poland.

Damages to be paid out by all insurance companies will total between one billion and 1.5 billion zlotys, up to 40 percent of which will be covered by reinsurers, PZU president Jan Monkiewicz said on Monday.
- Poland's biggest refinery Petrochemia Plock (PP) has increased its wholesale petrol price by 0.01 zloty per litre and diesel oil by 0.02 zloty per litre, the plant said.
Rafineria Gdansk (RG), the second biggest refinery, will probably raise fuel prices this week.
- The Bank of America will have to inject capital into Bank Zachodni in Wroclaw, southwestern Poland, to receive a central bank operating licence in Poland.
The central bank's decision must be confirmed by the finance ministry.
- Grain cargo made up the bulk of shipments by the Polska Zegluga Morska (PZM) shipping firm in the first half of 1997, PZM spokesman Krzysztof Gogol said.
Coal, coke and general cargo shipments grew in the period while shipments of iron ores and phosphorus compounds declined, Gogol said.

- Lascaridis Shipping, Eastwind and DSS have offered to buy a 70 percent share stake in the Transocean deep sea fishing firm in Szczecin, northwestern Poland, to be privatised by the end of 1997, the treasury ministry said.

- Around 30,000 of Poland's unemployed are helping to repair damages caused by floods in southern Poland, a number which could double, the cabinet minister in charge of anti-flood operations, Andrzej Pilat, said.

- Polish Energy Partners SA (PEP), a joint venture of the Polish Private Equity Fund and Polish Enterprise Fund, plans to invest at least $15 million in the development of the country's energy industry, PEP president Wojciech Cetnarski said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The Stocznia Gdynia shipyard will build a car-transporter vessel to carry 6,000 cars for Norway's Leif Hoegh and Co AS shipping firm worth $57 million zlotys, the yard said.

- The Prokom Software SA computer system integrator has contracted software made by the SAP integrated software maker which will allow Prokom to install the SAP R/3 integrated software for Polish industrial customers, Prokom said.
- Poland's furniture industry exported around 80 percent of production to EU markets in the last few years, a report by the wood technology institute in Poznan, western Poland, said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Rafako boiler maker's losses reached 12 million zlotys in the first half of 1997, the company said.
ZYCIE

- The 1997 net profit of the privately-owned Polsat television broadcaster will exceed the profits of the state- owned Telewizja Polska (TVP) by at least 60 million zlotys, PAI Media advertising agency president Piotr Fajs said.
